assumptions: The task formalizes the square case proved first in Lemma 4.1; the paper's later zero-column extension to rectangular matrices is outside this target.
P, Q, Sigma, fSigma, and the recovery diagonal record the SVD and pseudoinverse identities displayed between equations (4.5) and (4.6).
The scaled bound on the recovery multiplier is the direct quantitative form of condition (4.2).
The Hermitian-polar perturbation fields represent the conditioning fact explicitly invoked by the source proof.
The constants hidden by the paper's d-epsilon notation are exposed by p28CoreCoefficient; the two conclusions remain the residual and Hermitian-factor estimates (4.3)-(4.4).

formal_statement.plain_language: Under the mixed backward-forward, SVD recovery, mapping-gain, unitary, and Hermitian-polar perturbation relations used in the square-case proof of Lemma 4.1, the symmetrized factor has both the claimed small residual and the claimed small error from the Hermitian polar factor.

informal_proof: Equate the two expressions for the computed mapped matrix. Use the SVD and pseudoinverse diagonal identities to recover Xbar-UHbar from the mapped discrepancy and bound it with condition (4.2). Left-multiply by U-star, symmetrize, and combine unitary invariance, self-adjointness, and Hermitian-polar perturbation to obtain both conclusions.
informal_statement: The square-matrix proof core of Lemma 4.1, yielding equations (4.3) and (4.4) with the paper's suppressed constants made explicit.

tier_rationale: The source proof requires a noncommutative SVD/pseudoinverse recovery calculation, quantitative perturbation transport through a mapping gain, unitary norm invariance, Hermitian symmetrization, and two final factor bounds. This is substantial T2-or-harder polar-analysis work and is not solved by Mathlib imports. NumStability has no corresponding polar result, so L receives no material advantage over N.
